name: timer
title: Timer
description: A countdown that owns its own clock. It is a thin wrapper over stat, so the number, the tabular numerals and the accessible name are stat's; what it adds is the one thing stat refuses to do, which is perform. It holds the interval, reads the wall clock rather than counting ticks so a throttled tab catches up instead of losing seconds, keeps its place across a pause, clears itself on unmount, and calls the host back exactly once when time is up. `data-gs-value` is always seconds and never a formatted string, so a test reads 90 while a player reads 1:30. Critical is host-declared through a threshold in seconds, and it lands as a glyph, a text treatment and a changed accessible name, never as colour alone. It fixes `kind="timer"` so the host does not have to remember the kind, and `data-gs-component="timer"` identifies its root beside the score and round. It does not end the round or synchronise with a server. At expiry it stops its clock, marks itself complete and calls `onExpire` if supplied; the host decides what happens to play. Use plain `stat` with `kind="timer"` when the host already owns the clock and supplies the seconds, including time received from a server, so the display does not start a second clock. Draws as a filled pill whose fill changes at each threshold the host declares: running, warningAt, criticalAt. Three drawings rather than one drawing in three colours — a solid fill, an outline, then a solid fill in another hue with a glyph beside it — so a player who cannot tell the three apart by colour still sees three shapes.
docs: Pass `duration` in seconds and the component runs it; changing `duration` restarts the clock. Pass `direction="up"` to count elapsed rather than remaining, and note that either way the timer ends at the same moment, which is why `data-gs-direction` exists: one sample of `data-gs-value="90"` cannot say whether that is ninety elapsed or ninety remaining. Pass `criticalAt` to say how many seconds from the end counts as running out; leave it off and the timer is never critical, because the component does not guess where that line is. Pass `paused` to stop without finishing, which loses no time. Pass `onExpire` for the one call when time runs out. Pass `format` to render the seconds as something other than `m:ss`; `data-gs-value` still carries the seconds. An expired timer is `data-gs-complete="true"` with the value at the end of its range, and it is no longer critical, because time is not running out once it has run out. The group is not a live region, so the countdown is silent and a screen reader user reads the current time on demand rather than being read every second.
